title: Artificial Intelligence Powered Personal Finance Management System
authors: Chahar, P.; Vishwakarma, Y.K.; Mishra, R.; Paliwal, G.
tldr: An AI-powered personal finance management system combining Random Forest, SVM, and LSTM classifiers with a Flask-React web stack delivers automated expense categorization, predictive forecasting, and personalized budget recommendations, achieving high user satisfaction in preliminary evaluation.
problem_and_motivation: Existing personal finance tools rely on static rule-based methods and offer generic guidance, failing to adapt to individual spending behaviors or diverse income streams.
approach: A modular system architecture integrates data collection, expense classification, predictive analytics, recommendation, NLP interface, and security modules.
Supervised ML algorithms including Random Forest, Support Vector Machine, and LSTM networks trained on labeled transaction datasets.
Feature engineering uses transaction metadata with TF-IDF and word embeddings for text vectorization.
Time series forecasting models including ARIMA and LSTM applied to predict future expenses and cash flow trends.
Technology stack combines React.js for frontend UI, Flask for backend ML operations, MongoDB for data storage, and Firebase for authentication.
Security measures include end-to-end encryption, role-based access control, anonymization during training, and GDPR compliance.
findings: num: User survey yielded overall satisfaction rating of 4.4 out of 5 across financial management requirements.
Convenience of use received the highest user rating at 4.5 out of 5.
Goal-setting functionality received a user satisfaction score of 4.3 out of 5.
Transaction categorization correctness scored 4.2 out of 5.
System performed well for users with stable income but struggled with variable or irregular spending patterns.
Data quality directly impacted prediction accuracy.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: Contributes a comprehensive modular system design integrating multiple AI capabilities including expense classification, predictive analytics, recommendation, and NLP into a single personal finance platform. Provides systematic literature review of existing AI-powered personal finance tools.
directly_justifies: Machine learning algorithms such as decision trees, SVM, and neural networks categorize transactions with high accuracy.
Time series models including ARIMA and LSTM predict future expenses or cash flow trends.
Existing personal finance tools rely on static rules rather than adaptive learning models.
Consumer acceptability of AI finance tools varies significantly across demographics.
limits: Preliminary prototype lacks quantitative experimental comparison against established baselines.
No specific dataset size or benchmark accuracy numbers are reported for classification models.
System adaptability is limited for users with irregular or fluctuating income streams.
Paper does not address the cold-start problem for new users without historical data.
Evaluation relies primarily on user surveys rather than rigorous algorithmic benchmarking.
